diagrams.position: beside lines 13-22, right margin (the third figure runs slightly below line 22)
diagrams.description: Three similar figures stacked vertically, brown ink, thinner pen than the text (probably the scribe). Each = two parallel vertical lines, with a label row at the top (θ at the left line, the name of the interval in the middle, the smaller number at the right line) and a label between the lines at the bottom. Fig. 1 (beside ll. 13-15): top 'θ τόνο(ς) η' (τόν with small ο above ν); bottom 'ἐπόγδο(ος)' (stroke over δο; expansion -ος or -ον). Fig. 2 (beside ll. 16-19): top 'θ ἡμιεπ(όγδοον)[?] η' + a crescent-shaped sign with two dots above it after η (fraction ½: 8½); the middle word is ἡμι + a letter with a superscript N-like sign and acute (ἡμιεπ(όγδοον) or ἡμιτόν(ιον)); bottom, in two lines and partly in a brown stain: 'ἡμϊ ἐ- / π ὀκτ(ώ)' (= ἥμισυ ἐπ' ὀκτώ?). Fig. 3 (beside ll. 20-22 and below): top 'θ δίεσ(ις) ηδʹ' (δίεσ with superscript ι-like sign; δ with stroke = ¼: 8¼); bottom in two lines: 'ἐπ ὀκτὼ / τέταρτ(ον)'. The figures show the ratios 9 : 8 (tone), 9 : 8½ (semitone) and 9 : 8¼ (diesis) discussed in lines 14-22.

orthography: Careful 11th-c. minuscule with many majuscule forms (Δ in δέ/δι-, tall Τ, Η, Κ, Ν/N at line end, ΓΓ in φθόγγ-). ν is usually μ-shaped (u with a left descender), sometimes V-shaped; β is u-shaped; π sometimes ϖ-shaped. Frequent ligatures: στ, ετ (ε often a curl over τ, π or μ), ει (q-shaped, with the ι rising to the upper right), ευ, αυ, θε, σθ, γεω, ων (ν as a tall stroke from ω). Iota adscript is written only in τῆι (64r.20-21, 64v.16, 65v.5, 65v.8) and ὕληι (65r.19); elsewhere it is omitted (τῆ, μιᾶ, ἐπιτόμω, ὧ, γεωμετρία, πεντεκαιδεκαχόρδω, ἀριθμητικῆ, αὐτῆ). Breathings are small dots or wedges and rough and smooth are hardly distinguishable; they are transcribed in the expected form. Accentuation is fairly full but irregular: ἄν for ἂν (64r.7, 64r.12), ὀρθώς (64v.13), ἐστιν/ἐστι/τι and χρηστος unaccented, ἅπὰν (65v.6) and μοιρὰν (65r.21) with grave; ἡ/ἠ (ἢ) written with breathing only (64v.4, 65v.2, 65v.11). Grave also before punctuation (μουσικὴ., κὴ.). Diaeresis on ι: στϊγμή, διϊστάμενο(ν). Forms kept as written: ὑπάτη διάτονος (64v.19), διεζευγμένη for -ων (64v.21-22), ἑξκαιδέκατον (65v.13). Elision is written without an apostrophe in δ'ἄν and οὐδ'ἂν, with one in ἀλλ' and μεθ'. Punctuation: the high point is frequent; the low point (often after δὲ before a definition) and a comma (dot with a tail, at baseline) also occur. Words split at line end freely (κα|λῶς, οὐ|κ, ἀ|γαγεῖν). Ekthesis of large red initials (Μ 64r.2, Φ 64v.3). No itacistic spellings noticed in these folios.
